# Go 1.27: Upgrade Traps and New APIs

Read this for a `go 1.27` module or before moving a toolchain or `go` line to 1.27. Below, `json`
is `encoding/json`, `jsonv2` is `encoding/json/v2`, and `jsontext` is `encoding/json/jsontext`.

## Moving a Toolchain or `go` Line to 1.27

- **Removed `GODEBUG` settings:** `asynctimerchan` (1 or 2), `gotypesalias=0`, `tlsunsafeekm=1`,
  `tlsrsakex=1`, `tls3des=1`, `tls10server=1`, `x509keypairleaf=0`, `x509sha1=1`, and `tlskyber=0`
  fail the build in `go.mod` `godebug` or `//go:debug` and abort the binary at startup from the
  environment. Search deployment manifests, unit files, and CI config for `GODEBUG=` first.
- **Patch level:** run the newest 1.27 patch release; early ones carried compiler, runtime, and
  `net/http` bugs and a TLS ClientHello that some middleboxes reset.
- **cgo:** current patch releases reject `#cgo` flags `--sysroot`, `-target`, `-l:name`, `-l` values
  containing `:`, `=`, or a path separator, and `-gen-*`/`-gnat*`. A build that carried them fails
  after the upgrade.
- **gofmt:** output differs for some files. Reformat in one commit and run the same toolchain's
  `gofmt` locally and in CI, or the format check fails.
- **`compress/flate`:** bytes differ from 1.26, as do `gzip`, `zlib`, `archive/zip`,
  and `image/png`. Regenerate golden files; never hash or cache-key compressed bytes.
- **`go mod tidy`:** on a `go 1.27` module it merges `require` blocks into at most two.
- **Closures:** literal names changed and identical literals may share code. Never assert on
  their symbol names or compare function code pointers.
- **Tracebacks:** `go 1.27` modules print `pprof` goroutine labels in goroutine traceback headers
  (crash dumps, `runtime.Stack`). Keep IDs and tokens out of labels, or set
  `GODEBUG=tracebacklabels=0`.
- **`SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR`:** on Windows and macOS they now replace the platform verifier
  with the files they name. Check developer machines and CI agents for stray values, or set
  `GODEBUG=x509sslcertoverrideplatform=0`.
- **`net.UnixConn`:** reads return bare `io.EOF`; code matching `*net.OpError` stops matching.
- **HTTP/1 `Response.Body.Close`:** drains up to 256 KiB or 50 ms in the background. Plain
  `defer resp.Body.Close()` suffices.
- **HTTP/2 server:** honors client priority; `DisableClientPriority` restores round-robin.
- **`golang.org/x/net/http2`:** current releases built with Go 1.27 wrap `net/http`'s HTTP/2 (build
  tag `http2legacy` keeps the old code), and a second `ConfigureServer` on one `Server` panics.
  Retest custom HTTP/2 server or transport setup.
- **Platforms:** macOS 13 is the minimum; `go` cannot fetch bzr modules.

## `encoding/json` and `encoding/json/v2`

- **Plain `encoding/json` runs on the v2 engine** with the v1 options set, and output can still
  change: invalid UTF-8 is written as a literal U+FFFD, `float64` and `any` map keys marshal, and
  `Decoder.Token` after `More` on truncated input returns `*json.SyntaxError`, not `io.EOF`.
  Rerun golden-file and wire tests on upgrade. `GOEXPERIMENT=nojsonv2` restores the old engine;
  benchmark marshal-heavy paths before relying on the new one.
- **`json.RawMessage` and `jsontext.Value` are one type.** A type switch with both cases is a
  "duplicate case" compile error.
- **Remove experiment-era tags.** A `format:` option makes `json.Marshal` return an error; move
  that formatting into a custom marshaler. `unknown` and `inline` are silently ignored, so the
  field marshals under its Go field name; write `embed` alone, with no name or other option.
- **Match errors by type, never text.** `encoding/json` returns `*json.UnmarshalTypeError` and
  `*json.SyntaxError`; `encoding/json/v2` returns `*jsonv2.SemanticError` or
  `*jsontext.SyntacticError`, so `errors.As` targets break when a call site moves.
- **Migrate in two steps.** First pass `json.DefaultOptionsV1()` to `jsonv2.Marshal` and
  `jsonv2.Unmarshal`: output is identical to `encoding/json`. Then add later options that override
  one v1 behaviour at a time, such as `jsonv2.FormatNilSliceAsNull(false)`, testing after each.
- **Adopting v2 is a wire-contract change (Mandate 4),** never a side effect of a Go upgrade. Nil
  slices and maps marshal as `[]`/`{}` (`jsonv2.FormatNilSliceAsNull`, `FormatNilMapAsNull`); field
  names match case-sensitively (`jsonv2.MatchCaseInsensitiveNames`); duplicate object names and
  invalid UTF-8 are rejected (`jsontext.AllowDuplicateNames`, `AllowInvalidUTF8`).
- **Bare v2 defaults that fail or drift.** `time.Duration` is an error
  (`json.FormatDurationAsNano`); map order is random (`jsonv2.Deterministic(true)`); `[N]byte` is
  base64 (`json.FormatByteArrayAsArray`); a Go array needs a JSON array of the same length
  (`json.UnmarshalArrayFromAnyLength`); no HTML escaping (`jsontext.EscapeForHTML`); a syntax error
  can leave the target partly filled. Move `omitempty` on numbers, bools, pointers, and interfaces
  to `omitzero`, which means the same in both. `string` is valid only on number types, and a struct
  with no JSON-representable fields is an error.
- **Custom methods.** `MarshalJSONTo` beats `MarshalJSON`, and `json.Marshal` calls it too, so a
  dependency adding it changes your output. v2 calls pointer-receiver `MarshalJSON` even on
  non-addressable values. Only `MarshalJSONTo` and `UnmarshalJSONFrom` may return
  `errors.ErrUnsupported` to fall back to default encoding; call `jsonv2.MarshalEncode`
  instead of `MarshalJSONTo` directly.
- **Streams.** `jsonv2.UnmarshalRead` reads to EOF and takes one value; for NDJSON loop
  `jsonv2.UnmarshalDecode` on a `jsontext.NewDecoder` until `io.EOF`. `MarshalWrite` adds no
  newline. `Token.Int` returns `(int64, error)`. `jsontext` has no size-limit option: wrap
  untrusted bodies in `http.MaxBytesReader`.

## Generic Methods, `uuid`, and Other Additions

- **Generic method vs function:** a method may declare its own type parameters, for example a
  `Map[R any]` method on `List[E]` that takes a `func(E) R`. Use one when the operation belongs in
  the type's namespace or chains left to right; otherwise write a top-level generic function. Call
  it as `l.Map(f)` or take `List[int].Map[int]`.
- **No interface role:** a generic method never satisfies an interface, and interface methods
  cannot declare type parameters. Keep a method plain if the type must implement an interface
  through it; making it generic drops conformance, and the error shows at the use site.
- **Limits:** `reflect` does not list generic methods, so reflective registries miss them. A
  return type that re-wraps the receiver (`func (T[P]) m() T[T[P]]`) is rejected. Run linters
  on the first package that declares one before spreading it.
- **`uuid` version:** `New` is v4 now but may change; call `NewV4` or `NewV7` when the version
  matters, `NewV7` for time-ordered values. None returns an error.
- **`uuid` text and SQL:** JSON and text are 36-char lowercase. `Parse` accepts hyphenated,
  braced, `urn:uuid:` (lower-case prefix only), and 32-hex forms. `database/sql` writes text, so
  pass `u[:]` for a binary column; it scans text or 16 raw bytes. Scanning NULL into a bare
  `uuid.UUID` is an error; use `sql.Null[uuid.UUID]`.
- **From `github.com/google/uuid`:** `NewV7` has no error result; `NewString`, `Must`, `FromBytes`,
  `Validate`, `Version`, `URN`, `MarshalBinary`, `NullUUID`, `Scan`, and `Value` are absent; an
  empty-string or NULL scan no longer gives `Nil`.
- **Small additions:** `strings.CutLast` and `bytes.CutLast` replace `LastIndex` splits.
  `url.URL.Clone` and `Values.Clone` deep-copy. A struct-literal key may name a promoted field
  (`Gopher{Name: "x", Burrow: "y"}`) unless it crosses an embedded pointer. Generic
  functions infer type arguments in conversions, composite literals, and channel sends.
